correctness.rationale: Over characteristic two, the projective equation has odd degree q+3. Its derivatives show no singular points on x=0. In coordinates x=1, t=y/x, s=z/x and κ²=k, the scheme ideal is (A²,B²) for A=1+t*s^(q/2), B=t^((q+2)/2)+s+κ, because f_t=A², f_s=B² and Euler makes f redundant. A=B=0 reduces bijectively to H(s)=s^(r+1)+κ*s^r+1=0, r=q(q+2)/4 even; H(0)=1, H′=s^r imply r+1 simple nonzero roots. The Jacobian determinant of (A,B) is s^(q/2) nonzero at each root, making A,B regular parameters. Thus each completed Jacobian algebra is K[[A,B]]/(A²,B²) of length four and total length 4(r+1). Polynomial differentiations were spot-checked symbolically for q=2,4,8,16, not as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source singled out an even-characteristic pathology but only noted non-smoothness and changed families. The all-q all-k theorem determines how the pathology grows as a quadratic number of geometric singular points, each with uniform 4-dimensional Frobenius-thickened local Jacobian algebra; the exact total singular scheme length is a natural invariant for studying singular degenerations, equisingularity and obstruction to smooth plane-filling constructions. It is neither a one-off small-field enumeration nor just a restatement of non-smoothness.
